Two more stops on the suffix map, and they're related in a way that will make you smile: the path you travel, and the thing that made it happen.

-kurru / -gurru / -wurru → along, through:
You've had towards (-lili) and away-from (-ŋuru). Here's the missing direction: THROUGH.

Ḏiltjikurru ŋarra marrtjina → I was walking through the bush
manymakkurru dhukarrkurru → along the good road (adjective agreeing again!)

And you've already met it hiding inside a question word:
Nhäkurru nhe ga marrtji? → Where are you going? (literally: along-what?)

It stretches beautifully into channels that aren't paths at all:
Bäpa ga waŋa djimiṉḏi kurru → Father is talking on the wireless, literally THROUGH it. The radio is a path your voice walks along. English says on the radio and thinks nothing; Gupapuyŋu maps the medium as terrain.

Cause: because-of, marked with suffixes you already own:
How did something come about? Mark the culprit with the instrumental (-dhu/-thu/-yu/-y for things, -gala/-kala/-wala for people, Lessons 11-12), and for more abstract sources, -buy/-puy/-wuy (Lesson 18):

Nhaliy ŋayi rirrikthurrunanydja? → What has made him sick? (literally: by-what is he sick? As a result of what?)

There's no separate word for because of. Cause IS instrument, seen from further back. The stick you hit with, the sun you sickened by, the reason you acted from, one marking, one worldview: things happen BY MEANS OF other things. English's because of, from, due to, owing to collapse into machinery you learned weeks ago.

Bonus: counting times:
And -mirri (yes, that one) on a numeral gives you times:
Nhämunha'mirri ŋayi nhuna ŋäṉ'thurrunanydja? → How many times did he ask you?
märrma'mirri → twice (having-two, two-fold)

Twice is with-two-ness. Of course it is.

By now you can feel the deep pattern of this whole language: a small set of suffixes, each one a lens, and meaning made by pointing the lenses at new things. Paths become radios. Instruments become causes. Possession becomes repetition. Nothing is wasted. Everything is reused, the grammar itself practices what the culture knows about resources.
